name: Gmail
tagline: Create your own Google OAuth client for Gmail. Your scopes decide the review: sensitive takes days, restricted takes weeks plus a yearly CASA audit.

approvalWait.asStated: Sensitive: typically 3-5 business days. Restricted: can potentially take several weeks (FAQ: 6 weeks). Not guaranteed.

cost.asStated: Google charges no fee. Restricted scopes need a yearly CASA assessment; any lab fee is agreed with the assessor. No official price.

steps.title: Set up your Composio account
steps.when: Skip if you already have a Composio project and API key.
instructions: Sign up from the Composio login page.
Open Settings → API keys and copy a key.
Save it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY where your agent runs.
Stay in this project. Auth configs belong to one project.

problems.q: I can't find the API keys page
a: Open the API keys link above after signing in. It opens Settings → API keys for your current project.
If you have several projects, switch to the one you'll use for this agent first.

steps.title: Choose your Gmail scopes
instructions: List the Gmail tools your agent calls. Pick the narrowest scope for each. This choice decides your review path.
Non-sensitive (gmail.labels): no scope review.
Sensitive (gmail.send): scope review with a justification and demo video. Google says typically 3-5 business days.
Restricted (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, mail.google.com): scope review plus a yearly CASA security assessment.
Reading mail outside a Workspace add-on always needs a restricted scope. Send-only agents can stay on gmail.send.
Only your own Workspace org will use it? Choose Internal in Audience and skip verification.
Don't request scopes for future features. Google rejects scopes broader than what your app shows.

warnings.text: IMAP/SMTP need mail.google.com (restricted). Sending over SMTP alone fails review; use the Gmail API with gmail.send.
gmail.metadata can't fetch message bodies and can't be combined with readonly, modify or mail.google.com.

steps.unconfirmed: Composio's default Gmail scopes aren't published. We couldn't see them without logging in, so check them in your auth config.

problems.q: Can I avoid the CASA security assessment?
a: Only by dropping restricted scopes: gmail.send plus gmail.labels covers send-and-organize agents.
Or keep the app Internal to your Workspace org, or for personal use under the 100-user cap.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
instructions: In Google Cloud console go to IAM & Admin → Create a Project.
Enter a Project name. Edit the Project ID now if you want; it can't change later.
Under Location, pick your Workspace organization if you have one. Internal apps need it.
Click Create.
Use separate projects for testing and production. Google only reviews the production one.

problems.q: My organization isn't listed under Location
a: You're signed in with a personal Google account. Sign in with your Workspace account and try again.
Without an organization you can't pick the Internal audience later.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
instructions: Go to APIs & Services → Library, search Gmail API, and click Enable.
Or run the gcloud command below in the same project.

warnings.text: Contact tools (GMAIL_GET_CONTACTS, GMAIL_SEARCH_PEOPLE) use the People API. Enable it too if your agent uses them.
warnings.unconfirmed: Composio's tool docs mention the People API. We didn't test which APIs those tools need enabled.

problems.q: Tool calls fail with "Gmail API has not been used in project"
a: The Gmail API isn't enabled in the project that owns your OAuth client.
Enable it in that project, wait a few minutes, and retry.

steps.title: Set up Branding
instructions: Go to Google Auth Platform → Branding. If it says not configured yet, click Get Started.
Fill App name and User support email, pick an audience, add Contact information, accept the User Data Policy, click Create.
Back on Branding, add your App logo, App domain links and Authorized domains.
Add authorized domains before any URL that uses them.
Unsure of some links? Use placeholders now. They're required before verification.

fields.label: App name
fields.hint: Shown on consent only after brand verification

fields.label: User support email
fields.hint: Must be you or a Google Group you manage

fields.label: Application privacy policy link
fields.hint: Same domain as the home page

warnings.text: Don't use Google product names in the app name. Names like "Gmail for Android" are rejected.
Logo: square, 120×120 px, under 1 MB. Changing it later in production needs re-verification.

steps.title: Set the audience and test users
instructions: Go to Google Auth Platform → Audience.
External: any Google account. Starts in Testing.
Internal: only your Workspace org. No verification and no 100-user cap.
Under Test users click Add users, enter the Google accounts you'll test with, and Save.
Testing allows up to 100 test users. They see a warning, and access expires 7 days after consent.
Stay in Testing until you're ready to submit for verification.

warnings.text: External + Testing: refresh tokens expire after 7 days. Test users must reconnect every week.

a: Your app is External and in Testing, so Google expires test users' tokens 7 days after consent.
Reconnect the account for now. The 7-day expiry applies to Testing; it stops once you publish to In production.
Unverified sensitive or restricted scopes then show the unverified screen and count toward the 100-user cap.
Check the exact Google account is listed under Audience → Test users.
Workspace or Advanced Protection accounts can be blocked by their own policies. See the admin step.
Audience is Internal and the user isn't in your Google Cloud organization.
Use an account from your org, or switch the user type to External.

steps.title: Declare scopes in Data Access
instructions: Go to Google Auth Platform → Data Access → Add or Remove Scopes.
Add each Gmail scope you chose, then click Save.
Google sorts them into non-sensitive, sensitive and restricted. That's your review path.
Use the exact same scopes in your Composio auth config.

warnings.text: If your app requests scopes not listed here, users see the unverified app screen.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
instructions: Go to Google Auth Platform → Clients → Create Client.
Pick Web application and fill in the values below.
Under Authorized redirect URIs click Add URI and paste the Composio callback.
Click Create, then copy the Client ID and Client secret from the dialog.
Google won't show the secret again. Store it in a secret manager, never in git.
Redirect URI changes can take 5 minutes to a few hours to apply.

fields.label: Authorized redirect URIs
fields.hint: Must match your Composio auth config exactly

fields.label: Use this client for an AI-powered agent

warnings.text: "Use this client for an AI-powered agent" can't be changed after you create the client.
warnings.unconfirmed: Google doesn't say what this setting changes for consent or verification. We couldn't test it.

a: The redirect URI Composio sends isn't on your client's Authorized redirect URIs list.
Copy the Redirect URI from your Composio auth config into Google exactly. No trailing slash.
Saved it already? Changes can take a few hours to apply.

problems.q: I closed the dialog before copying the secret
a: Open the client and click Add Secret. A client can have two secrets.
Put the new one in your Composio auth config, then disable and delete the old one.
invalid_client: the client ID or secret in Composio is wrong. Re-copy both.
deleted_client: the client was deleted. Restore it within 30 days from Deleted credentials.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Gmail toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Use the values below, then paste your Client ID and Client secret.
Set the scopes to exactly what you declared in Data Access.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Set it explicitly. Must match Google's Authorized redirect URI.

fields.label: Scopes
fields.hint: Example. Use your list from Data Access.

warnings.text: Some Composio defaults still use /api/v1/auth-apps/add as the redirect. Set the v3 callback in both places.

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Gmail toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Gmail, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for gmail.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a Google account on your Test users list and open the link.
Expect Google's warning that the app is unverified. Testers can continue.
Your app name and logo show only after brand verification.
Run a Gmail tool such as GMAIL_GET_PROFILE to confirm access.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Google sign-in.

problems.q: Google says it hasn't verified this app
a: Expected while sensitive or restricted scopes are unverified. Testers can click through.
Outside Testing, every new user counts toward a lifetime cap of 100. Get verified before launch.
The client asks for scopes Google hasn't approved for it. Remove extra scopes from the auth config.
Or declare them in Data Access and submit them for verification.
admin_policy_enforced means the user's Workspace admin blocked it. See the next step.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.
The user's token is no longer valid: revoked access, password change, admin policy, or Testing's 7-day expiry.
Reconnect the account.

steps.title: Get Workspace admin approval
steps.when: Only if a user's Workspace admin restricts third-party apps (admin_policy_enforced or app blocked).
instructions: Send the admin your OAuth Client ID.
Admin opens Admin console → Security → Access and data control → API controls → Manage App Access.
They find your app and set access to Trusted or Specific Google data.
If their org set Gmail access to Restricted, Limited isn't enough. It must be Trusted or Specific Google data.

a: Their Workspace admin restricts which apps can use Gmail scopes.
Only that admin can trust your client ID. Google support can't override it.

steps.title: Route the callback through your domain
steps.when: Before verification. Google wants every redirect URI domain listed and verified as yours.
instructions: Add an endpoint on your domain that 302-redirects to the Composio callback, keeping the query string.
Set that endpoint as the Authorized redirect URI on your Google client.
Set the same URI as Redirect URI in your Composio auth config.
Add your domain under Branding → Authorized domains.

warnings.text: Return a 302. Don't fetch Composio's callback server-side; the browser must follow the redirect.

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't confirm whether Google reviewers reject a composio.dev redirect domain you can't verify. This avoids the question.

steps.title: Prepare for brand verification
steps.when: External apps that go to production, or that want their name and logo on the consent screen.
instructions: Verify every authorized domain in Google Search Console with a project Owner or Editor account.
Home page: public, on your domain, describes the app, links the privacy policy. A login page alone fails.
Privacy policy: same domain, same link as in Branding, says how you use, store and share Google user data.
Add the Limited Use statement below to your policy or a public FAQ.
On Branding click Verify Branding. The automated check usually takes a few minutes.

fields.label: Limited Use statement
fields.value: [App name]'s use of information received from Google APIs will adhere to Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

problems.q: Branding shows Need to fix issues
a: Click View issues to see the failed checks. Fix them, then click Request re-verification.
Think a finding is wrong? Choose "Request additional review" in the same panel.
Edits are locked while verification runs. Click Cancel to stop it, edit, then verify again.

steps.title: Brand verification review

wait.asStated: Automated: typically a few minutes. If it can't decide, manual review usually takes 2-3 business days.

instructions: When the status is Ready to publish, click Publish branding.
Publish within 7 days or the result expires and shows Need to re-verify.
Data access (scope) verification needs published branding first.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and demo video
steps.when: You use any sensitive or restricted Gmail scope.
instructions: Per scope, write the feature that uses it and why a narrower scope won't work. An agent can draft this.
Script the video: the full OAuth flow in English, then each scope's feature in use.
Show the app name on the consent screen and your client ID in the address bar.
Restricted scopes on an automation platform: show how workflows are built and where user data flows.
If user data trains a personalized AI model, show the user explicitly consenting to it.
Upload the video to YouTube with Visibility set to Unlisted.

fields.label: Justification template
fields.value: My app uses https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send to [feature] on the [screen] screen. A narrower scope won't work because [reason].

steps.title: Publish and submit for verification
steps.when: You use any sensitive or restricted Gmail scope with External users.
instructions: In Audience, click Publish app to move to In production. Google only reviews production apps.
Delete OAuth clients in this project that aren't ready for production.
Open Verification Center, check your details, add each scope justification and the YouTube link.
Submit, then watch the developer contact and support emails. Google asks follow-ups there.

warnings.text: Until approved, users see the unverified app screen and each new user counts toward a lifetime cap of 100.
Changing app name, logo, redirect URI, home page or privacy link later needs brand re-verification.

problems.q: Verified, but users still see the unverified screen
a: Your app requests a scope that wasn't approved. Compare Composio's scopes with Data Access.
Remove the extra scope, or add it and submit it for verification before using it.
Access to the unapproved scopes stops working. Read the email for the reason.
Fix it, select the scopes again and resubmit with all materials.

steps.title: Sensitive scope review
steps.when: Your most sensitive scope is sensitive (e.g. gmail.send), not restricted.

wait.asStated: Typically 3-5 business days (Google's FAQ estimates 10 business days, not guaranteed).

instructions: Track Data access status in Verification Center.
Reply to Google's emails fast. The review pauses while it waits for you.

steps.title: Restricted scope review
steps.when: You request any restricted scope (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, mail.google.com, …).

wait.asStated: Can potentially take several weeks (Google's FAQ estimates 6 weeks, not guaranteed).

instructions: Google checks your app is a permitted Gmail use case and meets Limited Use.
The security assessment is the last part. Google emails you when to start it.
Reply to Google's emails fast. The review pauses while it waits for you.

steps.title: Pass the CASA security assessment
steps.when: Restricted scopes, and Gmail data is accessed from or through a server. Expect this with Composio.
instructions: Wait for Google's email. Google, not you, decides your tier and assurance level.
Contact an authorized CASA lab. It tests your app at the assigned level (AL1 or AL2).
Fix the failed findings to receive a Letter of Validation (LOV).
Follow your notification email. CASA's Tier 2 self-scan is deprecated.
You pay the lab directly; Google charges no fee.
Existing certifications may shorten it through the CASA Accelerator.
Repeat every 12 months from your LOV date. Google emails when it's due.

warnings.text: Lab fees are set between you and the assessor. Neither Google nor CASA publishes a price.
warnings.unconfirmed: We found no official price. Get quotes from several authorized labs.

warnings.text: Keep extra Owners or Editors on the project so the yearly reassessment email isn't missed.

steps.unconfirmed: Google gives no effort estimate for CASA. The minutes are our rough guess. We assume Composio's server-side calls count.
